correctness.rationale: PASS. The directed Gaussian KL from hI to B^(−1) reduces exactly to (k/2)(ah−1−ln h−ell), where a is arithmetic precision mean, h harmonic inverse mean, ell mean log precision. Scale eigenvalues into [1,K]; differentiating in one eigenvalue gives positive second derivative (1/k)[(1−2/k)/x²+1/(k h² x⁴)+2(a−h^(−1))/x³] for k≥2, so each maximizing eigenvalue is 1 or K. Interior constant spectra have zero divergence and are excluded for fixed K>1. For multiplicity t=m/k this yields precisely Phi_K(t), with unique interior continuous maximum by endpoint derivative signs and strict convexity of Phi′. The grid extremum, k→∞ envelope and K→1 and K→∞ limits follow. The explicit positive definite 2×2 Lanczos block with nonzero residual 1/2 and direct-sum B yields Schur complement diag(1,B), so its matched bulk achieves the same KL bound without artificial zero coupling. Independent floating-point arithmetic confirmed K=4,k=10,m=4 value D/k≈0.171078599745388 and sampled 300 random precision spectra for K=5, k=3,5,10 stayed below sharp limit. These tests supplement exact calculus.
